newsitem.title: GERMANY: German parliament passes multimedia law.
newsitem.headline: German parliament passes multimedia law.

text.p: Germany's parliament Friday passed Internet-related legislation that sets standards for child protection in cyberspace and defines which activities require regulation.

The legislation distinguishes between traditional media forms that use the Internet, and should therefore fall under media rules, and new services, such as e-mail or video conferencing, that the government says should not be classified as media.
The Information and Communications Services Act, set to take effect August 1, is one of the first pieces of law that outlines a legal framework for the Internet.
"With this law we are taking on a vanguard position," said Justice Minister Edzard Schmidt-Jorzig. "Germany desparately needs to grasp its opportunities this time."

The law was passed in the lower house of parliament with the majority of the ruling centre-right coalition government. It must still pass in the upper house, which is controlled by the opposition Social Democrats before it can take effect. The upper house will vote on the bill on July 4.
